content.title: About
content.content: Buttermilk is a cultured dairy drink made from the fermentation of cream. It has a mild tangy flavor, creamy texture, and a characteristic buttery aroma. Traditionally it is enjoyed as a refreshing beverage or used in cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Buttermilk originated in Europe in the 19th century as a by‑product of butter making.
In the United States it is often served cold, sometimes spiced with cinnamon or ginger.
In many cuisines buttermilk is added to pancake or waffle batter to make them fluffier.
Buttermilk contains probiotic cultures that support gut health.
Traditional buttermilk is unsweetened, though many commercial versions contain a small amount of sweetener.

items.title: Rich in probiotics
items.content: Buttermilk provides live Lactobacillus cultures that help maintain a healthy intestinal microbiome.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The drink supplies calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with cream, buttermilk has moderate fat content, making it suitable for lighter diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Its acidity stimulates gastric juice production, helping the digestion of food.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience bloating, gas, or diarrhea after consuming buttermilk.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergic reactions to casein or whey proteins can occur in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some commercial buttermilk products contain added salt, which should be considered by those with hypertension.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: Improper storage can lead to bacterial growth; always keep it refrigerated.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Buttermilk can be drunk chilled, blended into smoothies, added to baking batters, or used in sauces and marinades. It also pairs well with fruit, honey, or spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store buttermilk in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C in a sealed container. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if it develops off‑odors, mold, or discoloration.
